# CANDIDATE: BULLISH_RECLAIM_LOWER_HIGHS_ROLE_REVERSAL

**Filed:** 2026-09-08
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)
**Type:** new_trigger
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis
We hypothesize that a bullish reclaim is more likely to produce a sustained move when the prior three bounces at the support level were lower highs (indicating distribution and weakening bullish pressure) and the reclaimed level has just flipped from resistance to support (role reversal). This combination suggests sellers are exhausted and the level is now acting as support.

## Mechanism
Trigger conditions (all must be true on the 3-minute timeframe):
1. Bullish reclaim: price tests a defined support level (e.g., prior low, ascending trendline, premarket low) and closes above it on the reclaim bar.
2. Prior three bounces: the three most recent bounces (price touching the support level without closing below it) before the reclaim bar each formed a lower high than the previous bounce.
3. Role reversal: the reclaimed level was acting as resistance (price failed to break above it on at least two occasions) within the last 50 bars prior to the reclaim bar.
Entry: at the open of the bar immediately following the reclaim bar.
Stop: chart stop below the reclaimed level by $0.50 (or the nearest swing low, whichever is closer) - using same chart-stop logic as existing BULLISH_RECLAIM setup.
Exit: same as BULLISH_RECLAIM_RIDE_THE_RIBBON (ride the EMA ribbon, TP1 at +100% premium, runner, etc.).
